summary.headline: NCC Q2 FY27 console turnover rose 32% to Rs 6,042 crore, but FY27 guidance of 8-10% growth was retained.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 turnover was Rs 6,042 crore, up 32% YoY from Rs 4,585 crore, with EBITDA margin of 8.48% versus 7.45% a year earlier. H1 console turnover was Rs 11,884 crore, up 21%. Order book stood at Rs 80,167 crore at end-September 2026, with Q2 inflows of Rs 838 crore and October-to-date inflows bringing FY27 total to about Rs 11,108 crore (roughly 50% of the lower end of the Rs 22,000-25,000 crore guidance). Management retained full-year FY27 revenue growth guidance of 8-10% and did not raise it, while working capital days and unbilled revenue improved.

segments.name: Standalone vs subsidiaries order book
segments.commentary: Of the Rs 80,167 crore order book, Rs 71,293 crore sits in standalone and Rs 8,874 crore in subsidiaries; mining accounts for about Rs 5,923 crore of the total per the call.

segments.name: Smart meters (BOOT/HAM model)
segments.commentary: About 51% of smart meter installation is complete and 49% outstanding; payment comes in two phases, part at installation and balance monthly over 93 months, with no working capital issues reported.

segments.name: Jal Jeevan Mission
segments.commentary: Legacy JJM backlog in UP of about Rs 3,200 crore expected to be substantially completed by March 2027; current JJM project around Rs 2,128 crore. Trade receivables from JJM fell to Rs 344 crore from about Rs 2,700 crore last quarter per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 8-10% retained; management declined to comment on Q3 performance, calling it premature.
FY27 order inflow guidance of Rs 22,000-25,000 crore retained; Rs 11,108 crore achieved so far, about 50% of the lower band.
FY27 capex budget Rs 500 crore; Rs 253 crore spent in H1, with balance around Rs 250 crore expected in H2.
FY28 capex expected to be similar, driven by mining projects in Jharkhand and Amarpali.
Management targets return of working capital days to March 2026 level (about 68 days noted in call) by end FY27.
Expects Rs 270 crore Vizag land sale receivable to be recovered by end of the quarter.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex of Rs 253 crore against Rs 500 crore full-year budget; Q2 capex Rs 83 crore.
TBM (tunnel boring machine) capitalised and put to use from September 2026; depreciation expected to rise in Q3 and Q4 with TBM and mining capex.
Mining projects (Jharkhand, Amarpali) are capital intensive and will require capex in FY28.
Investment property under construction of Rs 107-108 crore relates to a Hyderabad project stalled by developer issues, under NCLT/RERA proceedings; management says investment is secured.
demand_pricing: Retention money rose to about Rs 2,500 crore (13.3% of revenue) versus about 8.5% a year-and-a-half earlier; increase of about Rs 150 crore QoQ attributed to electrical division contracts (up to 20%) and Mumbai city road contracts.
Around 81% of contracts have price variation clauses, which management says offset raw material price increases.
About 60% of clients are PSUs; government payment cycles range 50-60 days from bill certification, per management.
Bharatnath project executed about 11% of contract in MP and Uttarakhand, with about Rs 1,000 crore of work done; billing-to-realisation lead time is longer there.
Unbilled revenue fell QoQ, which management attributes to EPC milestone billing; Ken Betwa project unbilled revenue added under Ind AS 115 on certified spend (contract value Rs 3,389 crore to NCC).
Management cited a pipeline of about Rs 2.5 lakh crore of prospective projects.

qa_highlights.question: Why retain 8-10% FY27 growth guidance despite 21% H1 growth, implying a sharp H2 slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is for the full year, based on detailed project-level estimates; it is premature to discuss Q3 and it retained 8-10% growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why is retention money rising and can it be reduced?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said newer contracts carry 5% retention, with some electrical contracts up to 20%; retention can be replaced with bank guarantees (50% on some contracts), but will remain in the near term.

qa_highlights.question: Trade receivables and working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said trade receivables fell to Rs 344 crore and unbilled revenue to Rs 2,009 crore (prior-quarter figures as stated); expects working capital days to return toward March 2026 levels by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is H1 capex Rs 253 crore standalone only and what about CBM?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed Rs 253 crore for H1 at standalone level; CBM investment was capitalised in FY26 and is excluded.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook on JJM payments and backlog?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said JJM payments are improving and legacy UP backlog should be largely executed by March 2027; new JJM projects in other states are being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: Smart meter payment cycle and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: No working capital challenge: part payment at installation, balance monthly over 93 months after installation; payments regular.

qa_highlights.question: Finance cost and depreciation trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance cost has run at about Rs 166 crore per quarter for two quarters and is expected to continue; depreciation rising from Q3 due to TBM and mining capex, all in standalone.

risks_watch: Guidance of 8-10% growth implies a sharp H2 slowdown from H1's 21%; Q3 execution is the key test.
Retention money of about Rs 2,500 crore (13.3% of revenue) ties up cash and is rising.
Unbilled revenue and Bharatnath/Ken Betwa milestone billing; long billing-to-realisation lead time.
Rising depreciation and finance cost from TBM and mining projects will pressure margins in Q3 and Q4.
Hyderabad investment property (about Rs 107 crore) stuck in NCLT/RERA proceedings; timing of resolution uncertain.
Capex execution: Rs 250 crore balance to be spent in H2 against Rs 500 crore budget.
summary.management_tone: Confident on reported numbers and order inflow, but guarded on H2 revenue: management repeatedly declined to explain why guidance was not raised and called Q3 premature. Answers on the Ken Betwa value and smart meter split were vague or deferred offline.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 8-10% (midpoint 9%) retained despite H1 console turnover up 21% and Q2 up 32%; backing is partial, with Rs 80,167 crore order book (about 3.5x trailing revenue), Rs 11,108 crore FY27 inflows to date (about 50% of the lower band of the Rs 22,000-25,000 crore order inflow guidance), and a TBM in use since September 2026, but no specific capacity additions with numbers

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 8.48% from 7.45% YoY, but rising depreciation and finance cost (about Rs 166 crore per quarter) from TBM and mining capex will pressure Q3 and Q4 margins.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: TBM capitalised and in use from September 2026, and mining projects in Jharkhand and Amarpali are planned, but no capacity numbers were given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 console turnover rose 21% and Q2 rose 32%, yet FY27 guidance of 8-10% implies a sharp H2 slowdown, and management called Q3 premature to discuss.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY28 capex is expected to be similar to FY27's Rs 500 crore, driven by mining projects in Jharkhand and Amarpali, which are capital intensive.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management retained 8-10% FY27 revenue growth despite H1 growth of 21%, and did not raise it.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Guidance of 8-10% implies H2 growth far below H1's 21%, and order inflow is at about 50% of the lower band of the Rs 22,000-25,000 crore target with Q3 execution still unproven.

rows.label: Working capital days return to ~68 (March 2026 level) by end FY27
rows.why: Net working capital days fell to 53 from 68 in Q1 and 78 a year earlier, and management targets a return to the March 2026 level, though retention money has risen to about Rs 2,500 crore (13.3% of revenue).

rows.label: FY27 order inflow guidance of Rs 22,000-25,000 crore
rows.why: Rs 11,108 crore achieved so far, about 50% of the lower band, and the Q2 inflow was only Rs 838 crore, so meeting the target needs a large H2 pickup.

rows.label: Vizag land sale receivable of Rs 270 crore
rows.why: Management expects the Rs 270 crore Vizag land sale receivable to be recovered by the end of the quarter, which would ease cash flow.

tone.note: Management was confident on reported growth, order inflow and working capital, but guarded on H2 revenue and repeatedly declined to explain why guidance was not raised; analysts pressed on the implied H2 slowdown.
